This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Project

LaTeX source for "Spectral-R1: Latent Energy-Based Verifiable Reward for Online RL without Labels" — NeurIPS 2026 submission.

Core claim: Spectral structure in the latent space of a policy's rollouts provides a verifiable reward signal without ground-truth labels, enabling online RL where outcome supervision is unavailable.

Paper plan: `self-reward-plan.md`

### Lineage

This paper evolves from the Spectral-R1 line of work:
- Previous paper repo: `../s_cot_tex` (NeurIPS 2025 submission — agentic decoding + energy-based OT)
- Training code: `../s_cot_tex/s_cot/` and remote `kurkin-1:/workspace-SR004.nfs2/kurkin/s_cot`
- Governance/bot: `../ourosss`

## Build

```bash
make # Full build: pdflatex + bibtex (3-pass)
make clean # Remove aux files
make distclean # Remove aux + PDF
```

Requires pdflatex and bibtex. Style file: `neurips_2026.sty` (included, based on neurips_2025.sty).

## Structure

```
main.tex — entry point; \input{sections/XX_name}
references.bib — BibTeX references
neurips_2026.sty — NeurIPS style file
sections/
 00_abstract.tex — abstract
 01_introduction.tex — introduction
 02_related_work.tex — related work
 03_method.tex — method (spectral verifier, training objective, GORE)
 04_experiments.tex — experiments and ablations
 05_discussion.tex — discussion and limitations
 06_conclusion.tex — conclusion
 07_appendix.tex — appendix
figures/ — figures directory
```

## LaTeX Conventions

- One sentence per line in .tex files (clean diffs)
- `\input{sections/XX_name}` for all sections — do not inline content in main.tex
- Use `[preprint]` option during development; switch to `[final]` for camera-ready
- Figures go in `figures/` directory

## Git Conventions

- Commit prefixes: `[paper]` for content, `[fig]` for figures, `[bib]` for references
- `fixes #N` in commits to auto-close issues

## Key Technical Concepts

- **Spectral Verifier**: reward signal derived from spectral structure of rollout representations (eigenspectrum of latent matrix), r(x) = -E(z)
- **GRPO base**: Group Relative Policy Optimization with spectral reward replacing/augmenting outcome reward
- **GORE**: formal language with deterministic interpreter used as controlled experimental environment
- **KL regularization**: precision-weighted KL penalty (connection to predictive processing / active inference)
- Base models: Qwen3-1.7B, Qwen3-7B with LoRA (r=16)

## Key References

- DeepSeek-R1 (Guo et al., 2025) — verifiable outcome reward
- GRPO / DAPO / Dr.GRPO — policy optimization baselines
- Let's Verify Step by Step (Lightman et al., 2023) — process reward
- Math-Shepherd (Wang et al., 2024) — process reward without annotations
- DIAYN (Eysenbach et al., 2018) — intrinsic reward baseline
- Active Inference / FEP (Friston) — intro analogy only
